title: if
goal: In this lesson you will learn how an if statement runs code only when a condition is True.
idea: An if statement checks a condition. If it is True, Python runs the indented block underneath. If it is False, Python skips that block. Always end the if line with a colon :. Indent the lines that belong to the if (usually 4 spaces). Only one path runs for that if. When the condition is true.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change score = 90 to score = 100. Press Run. You should see both Great job! and Perfect score!.

practice.text: If temp is greater than 30, print Hot day. Set temp to 35.
practice.hint: Write if temp > 30: with a colon, then indent the next line with 4 spaces. Only that indented line runs when the condition is True.
practice.starterTip: After the comment, add if temp > 30: and on the next line (indented) print("Hot day").
practice.gradingNote: Pass if if temp > 30: prints Hot day (indentation required).

practice.text: Set lives = 0. If lives equal 0, print Game over. Also print Done after the if.
practice.hint: Use == to check if lives equals 0. Put the if block between lives and the Done print. Done should not be indented under the if.
practice.starterTip: Add if lives == 0: with an indented print("Game over") above print("Done") so Done always runs.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if if lives == 0 prints Game over, then Done outside the if.

quiz.question: What must come at the end of an if line?
When does the indented block under if run?

options.text: Only when the condition is True
Only when the condition is False

quiz.correct: The block runs only if the condition is True.
quiz.wrong: False conditions skip the indented lines.

quiz.question: Why indent under if?

options.text: It tells Python which lines belong to the if

quiz.wrong: Without indent, Python does not know what belongs to the if.
